title: fix(ios): calendar, reminders and motion reject timestamps with fractional seconds
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on iOS nodes, `calendar.add` fails with `CALENDAR_INVALID: startISO required` and `reminders.add` fails with `REMINDERS_INVALID: dueISO must be ISO-8601` when the timestamp has fractional seconds, for example `2026-11-08T10:00:00.000Z`, which is what JavaScript's `toISOString()` produces. `calendar.events` and `motion.activity` / `motion.pedometer` are also affected: they silently ignore such a `startISO`/`endISO` and query their default range instead. Android accepts the same values (`Instant.parse`).

## User Impact

User impact: calendar, reminder and motion commands on iOS accept ISO 8601 instants with or without fractional seconds, matching Android. Output timestamps are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each service parsed with `ISO8601DateFormatter()` using its default options, which reject fractional seconds. A new `OpenClawISO8601.date(from:)` in OpenClawKit tries `[.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]` first, then the default form. Calendar (`add` and `resolveRange`), reminders (`applyDueISO`) and motion (`resolveRange`) now parse through it.

## Evidence

Standalone run of the helper file from this branch against the default formatter used on `main`:

```text
2026-11-08T10:00:00Z             main: 1794132000.0  fix: 1794132000.0
2026-11-08T10:00:00.000Z         main: nil  fix: 1794132000.0
2026-11-08T15:30:00.000+05:30    main: nil  fix: 1794132000.0
2026-11-08T10:00:00.250Z         main: nil  fix: 1794132000.25
                                 main: nil  fix: nil
tomorrow at 10                   main: nil  fix: nil
2026-11-08                       main: nil  fix: nil
```

- `OpenClawISO8601Tests` (Swift Testing, OpenClawKitTests) covers the same cases.
- `swift build --target OpenClawKit` compiles the new file.
- Gap: I could not run the full OpenClawKitTests bundle or build the iOS app here (Command Line Tools only; `OpenClawChatUI` needs Xcode's SwiftUI macro plugin), so CI is the first run of the test and the iOS call sites.


## Simulator proof through the iOS node

In an iOS 27.2 Simulator, `calendar.add`, `calendar.events` and `reminders.add` sent through `NodeAppModel.handleInvoke` against live EventKit now accept fractional-second timestamps; whole-second input still works. Before the fix, fractional `calendar.add` failed with `CALENDAR_INVALID` and `reminders.add` with `REMINDERS_INVALID`. `OpenClawISO8601Tests` fails on the old parsing (3 issues) and passes on this head. Core Motion is not available in the Simulator, so `motion.activity` could not be exercised live; no physical device was used. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195351#issuecomment-6744528705
